newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern reaffirms Conrail offer.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern reaffirms Conrail offer.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said on Tuesday that it reaffirmed its all-cash $100 per share offer for Conrail.
The company also said it terminated its talks with CSX Corp. Norfolk Southern and CSX are competing to buy Philadelphia-based Conrail.
On October 23, Norfolk launched an unsolicited $100 per share bid for Conrail and then sued to block the proposed $8.4 billion friendly merger between CSX and Conrail.

"Let there be no misunderstanding and no disinformation: We are committed to taking every necessary step to provide Conrail shareholders with the choice of our better offer," said David Goode, chairman and chief executive of Norfolk Southern.
The company said its offer would close to a voting trust, providing immediate cash payment to all shareholders.
Goode said the company stopped talking to CSX, based in Richmond, Virginia, because it was a waste of time.
"Until CSX acknowledges that all Conrail shareholders are entitled to the $100 cash that they can only receive from Norfolk Southern's offer, any discussions between us are a waste of time," he said.
